tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description does not use literal 'Use this skill when' phrasing but functions imperatively via the gerund-form opener ('Triage a live failure...') directed at the agent, and extensively enumerates concrete trigger contexts (5xx, throttling, timeouts, degraded TTFT, empty responses, post-deploy failures, dependency breaks, bare status questions) as well as explicit exclusions ('Do not load it for a symptom that names no model call'). It focuses on the user's actual situation (a live failure with a model call in the path) rather than internal implementation, and while detailed, it is a single dense paragraph appropriate for the complexity of the triage scope it covers.
tests.evidence: Triage a live failure where a model call is in the failing path - Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker endpoints, Bedrock AgentCore, or a model self-hosted on EC2, ECS, EKS or Lambda - and rule whether the fault sits with the provider, the customer's infrastructure or the application before any fix is prescribed.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but almost entirely domain-specific — classifier rules, locus tokens, ladder logic, guardrails specific to this skill's incident-triage procedure. It does not explain generic concepts like what Bedrock or CloudWatch are; it assumes that knowledge and jumps to non-obvious conventions (token sets, UNDETERMINED entrances, check-ids).
tests.evidence: "Two closed token sets. locus is PROVIDER, INFRASTRUCTURE, APPLICATION or UNDETERMINED..." — this is project-specific convention, not general knowledge.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (error code tables, metric thresholds, API call lists) is consistently pushed to references/ files and linked conditionally rather than embedded as large blocks in the body. The body contains rules and a ladder but these are the compact decision logic itself, not a reference dump.
tests.evidence: "The detail of every step, with its branches and forbidden exits, is in classifier-walkthrough.md; API arguments and rationale are in transient-vs-config-classifier.md."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file under references/ has a markdown link in the body (verified api-quirks.md, checks-telemetry.md, classifier-walkthrough.md, collection-reference.md, common-wrong-answers.md, error-codes.md, hosting-bindings.md, incident-signatures.md, metrics-and-logs.md, related-skills.md, request-path.md, router.md, severity-definitions.md, transient-vs-config-classifier.md all appear as links).
tests.evidence: "[hosting-bindings.md](references/hosting-bindings.md) — **Step 0**: the signal triple..." and similar links for all 14 reference files in the References section.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Reference links are consistently accompanied by specific trigger conditions explaining when to load them, both inline in the body and in the final References list.
tests.evidence: "If the condition is unmet... The ladder in this skill rules on three signals whose metric names differ per hosting, so bind first: [hosting-bindings.md](references/hosting-bindings.md)."

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/<filename>.md with no absolute paths or traversals.
tests.evidence: "[router.md](references/router.md)" — consistent relative path format used throughout.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (the classifier ladder, token sets, guardrails) are given exact prescriptive rules, while softer judgment areas (how to conclude, how to weigh evidence, related skills) are described with rationale rather than rigid steps, matching prescriptiveness to fragility.
tests.evidence: "The ladder is total; the first rule that holds wins." paired with "Commit to the most likely cause; do not leave it a hypothesis... When the evidence fits one cause and contradicts the alternatives, state it as the most likely cause."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple hosting/tooling paths exist, the skill designates defaults (e.g., AWS/Bedrock as default binding) and treats others as explicit alternates with their own bindings, rather than presenting them as an undifferentiated menu.
tests.evidence: "Name the binding in the payload: a gatherer told nothing about hosting defaults to AWS/Bedrock."

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable classifier procedure (bind, measure, correlate, rule) applicable to any incident matching the load condition, not a one-off instance; specific tokens/templates are details within a reusable approach.
tests.evidence: "Work the steps in order and track progress against this checklist... Step 1: Check provider health... Step 6: Rule by the total precedence ladder R1→R5..."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has extensive gotchas-style content under 'Error Handling' and throughout (e.g., CloudWatch no-datapoints misreading, agent PREPARED vs serving version, guardrail intervention spikes) — exactly the non-obvious environment-specific corrections this test looks for.
tests.evidence: "CloudWatch "no datapoints" ≠ zero (§10)... Agent PREPARED ≠ what the alias serves (§6)... Guardrail InvocationsIntervened high ≠ broken guardrail (§11)."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill's purpose clearly implies structured output (a TRIAGE line, Findings block) and it provides both inline minimal structure and a dedicated template asset for the longer form.
tests.evidence: "[triage-report-template.md](assets/triage-report-template.md) is the long form of the same shape, for when a full written report is wanted."

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body does not embed a large inline template; it specifies short contract requirements (three blocks: TRIAGE line, prose, Findings block) and defers the full long-form template to assets/triage-report-template.md.
tests.evidence: "Exit: three blocks, every time. The TRIAGE: line first, then the prose, then the Findings block with one line per signal."

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Both files in assets/ (delegation-payload.json and triage-report-template.md) are linked in the body.
tests.evidence: "[delegation-payload.json](assets/delegation-payload.json) is that prompt, finished: read it, fill the four <…> placeholders" and "[triage-report-template.md](assets/triage-report-template.md), *Short form*)"

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Both asset links specify clear trigger conditions for when to load them (delegating evidence-gathering work; rendering the final three blocks).
tests.evidence: "When you hand evidence-gathering to a sub-agent... [delegation-payload.json](assets/delegation-payload.json) is that prompt, finished: read it, fill the four <…> placeholders... send it unchanged."

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: Both asset references use relative paths in the form assets/<filename> with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The classifier procedure is presented as a checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' labels, and the detailed walkthrough file is described as expanding 'every step' from that same checklist, satisfying the step-numbering linkage requirement.
tests.evidence: "- [ ] Step 0: **Bind.**... - [ ] Step 1: Check provider health... - [ ] Step 6: Rule by the total precedence ladder R1→R5..."

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an extensive explicit self-validation section instructing the agent to re-check its own classifier output against a detailed checklist before presenting results.
tests.evidence: "Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output... Before you present a triage result, re-check your own classifier output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion."
